methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study an accurate model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the relationship and then repairing it helps expose missing links and build a more usable mental model.
how: Answer in your own words without copying the phrasing.
Compare your answer with the model and notice what is missing or unclear.
Fix one specific gap, then explain it again from memory.
methodBriefing.completion: You can explain each rule correctly, identify the key relationship, and give a correct example or application.
personalization: Start with the big picture before details.
Use one step at a time.
Restore support in smaller steps after a miss.

activities.label: model_1
activities.title: Product rule basics
activities.body: Read the model and note the rule structure.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second factor and the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.

activities.label: check_1
activities.title: Explain the product rule
activities.body: State the rule in your own words and then solve one product derivative.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x). For example, if y = x^2 sin x, then y' = 2x sin x + x^2 cos x.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms in the product rule and applies them to one product. A common gap is changing only one factor or multiplying the derivatives together.

activities.label: model_2
activities.title: Chain rule basics
activities.body: Read the model and track outer, inner, then multiply.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a composite function by taking the derivative of the outer function at the inner function and multiplying by the inner derivative.

activities.label: check_2
activities.title: Explain the chain rule
activities.body: Restate the rule in plain language and apply it once.
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outside function and multiply by the derivative of the inside function. For example, if y = (3x+1)^4, then y' = 4(3x+1)^3 · 3.
activities.feedback: A complete answer identifies outer and inner parts and multiplies by the inner derivative. A common gap is differentiating only the outside part and stopping there.

activities.label: check_3
activities.title: Choose the right rule
activities.body: Pick the derivative method that fits the expression.
choices: Use the chain rule because one function is inside another.
Use the product rule because two functions are being multiplied.
Use the quotient rule because one expression is on top of another.
Use only the power rule because the expression has an exponent.
activities.correctAnswer: Use the chain rule because one function is inside another.
activities.feedback: The chain rule applies to a composition, while the product rule applies to a product of factors. The key question is whether one function is inside another.

items.essentialIdea: Differentiate a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second factor and the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.

check.title: Explain the product rule
check.prompt: State the rule in your own words and then solve one product derivative.
check.referenceAnswer: The derivative of a product is f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x). For example, if y = x^2 sin x, then y' = 2x sin x + x^2 cos x.
check.feedback: A complete answer names both terms in the product rule and applies them to one product. A common gap is changing only one factor or multiplying the derivatives together.

items.essentialIdea: Chain rule differentiates a composite by multiplying outer and inner derivatives.

check.title: Differentiate a composite
check.prompt: How do you differentiate y = f(g(x))?
check.referenceAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at g(x), then multiply by g'(x): y' = f'(g(x))g'(x).
check.feedback: The outer derivative stays evaluated at the inner function, then you multiply by the inner derivative.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify the chain rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which derivative rule applies to y = f(g(x))?
choices: Differentiate the outer function at g(x), then multiply by g'(x).
Multiply f(x) and g(x) first, then differentiate the result.
Differentiate each function separately and add the derivatives.
Differentiate the inner function first, then subtract it from the outer derivative.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at g(x), then multiply by g'(x).
recognitionCheck.feedback: This is the chain rule because the function is composite.
